references.title: LMFDB, Elliptic curve 1611.a1 over Q
references.note: Minimal model y^2 + y = x^3 - 9x + 20; Cremona 1611d1, conductor 1611 = 3^2·179, rank 2, trivial torsion; short model y^2 = x^3 - 144x + 1296. Lists exactly the 22 integral points of this node's conclusion.

references.title: È. T. Avanesov, Solution of a problem on figurate numbers (Russian), Acta Arith. 12 (1966/67) 409–420
references.note: Solved C(n,2) = C(m,3) completely; this curve is that equation under x = 3(m-1), y = 9n - 5 (the parent's assembly). Cited through BBdW 2017's proof of Thm 2.2; not opened here.

references.title: R. J. Stroeker, N. Tzanakis, Solving elliptic diophantine equations by estimating linear forms in elliptic logarithms, Acta Arith. 67 (1994) 177–196
references.note: The method by which integral points of a rank-r elliptic curve are determined completely (Baker-type lower bound, then LLL reduction); implemented in Sage and Magma.

summary: Known. The integral points of the elliptic curve 1611.a1 (y^2 + y = x^3 - 9x + 20) are a published computation: the LMFDB lists exactly the 22 in this node's conclusion, found from a Mordell–Weil basis by the elliptic-logarithm method. Not formalised: a Lean proof would need the Mordell–Weil group and a Baker-type bound. This node is the whole number-theoretic content of its parent; the parent's assembly, which maps the binomial equation onto this curve, is proved.
model_and_tooling: Claude Opus 5.5 through Claude Code; LMFDB curve pages read 2026-10-29; point lists re-checked in Python (each point satisfies the equation, and a search over |x| <= 3e6 finds no other)
